name: INSACERMO_NASA_CMAPSS_FD001_BLIND_PLANNER_PREREG_V1
purpose: First pre-specified INSACERMO planner test outside the ASlib solver-selection meta-domain, using NASA C-MAPSS aerospace predictive-maintenance data.

source_metadata.selection_rule: Use FD001 because it is the first listed C-MAPSS subset in NASA metadata and has one operating condition and one fault mode. Selection is based only on NASA metadata, before opening test RUL values.

instance_definition: One instance is one FD001 test engine at its last observed cycle. Only that final-cycle pre-decision state is used for the primary planner.

outcome.name: true_remaining_useful_life_cycles
outcome.role: Used only after preregistration to assign Good maintenance actions; never used to choose probes or thresholds.

maintenance_contract.status: hypothetical structural stress-test contract, not an aviation standard or operational recommendation
maintenance_contract.threshold_selection: Fixed round thresholds chosen prospectively for a three-zone structural test; not estimated from FD001 outcomes.

capabilities.interpretation: REPAIR adds the missing intermediate maintenance capability. Base may therefore be capability-incomplete for worlds whose true RUL lies in the planning window.

probe_library.selection_rule: Use the first 10 pre-decision variables after unit_id and cycle in the official C-MAPSS column order: operational settings 1-3 followed by sensors 1-7.
probe_library.coarsening: Numeric quartile bins computed from the 100 final-cycle feature values only; duplicate cuts collapsed; no RUL values used to define bins.

population: All 100 FD001 test engines with complete final-cycle rows and a corresponding true RUL value. No base-actionable filtering is applied because capability incompleteness is itself part of the primary test.
safe_representation: Every realized observation cell induced by selected probes must admit at least one common Good action from the current capability set for every engine in that cell.

planner.search: Exhaustive over 2^10 probe subsets under base and repaired capability sets.
planner.optimal_frontier: All globally minimum-cost safe states; ties retained.

primary_endpoints: route regime among ACT, PROBE, REPAIR, PROBE+REPAIR, REFUSE
whether REPAIR converts capability-unreachable worlds into a reachable safe representation
secondary_endpoints: counts of engines in each frozen RUL action zone

frozen_route_rules.ACT: Base with zero probes is safe.
frozen_route_rules.PROBE: A minimum-cost safe terminal exists without REPAIR and uses at least one probe.
frozen_route_rules.REPAIR: Base zero-probe is unsafe and REPAIR with zero probes is safe and globally minimum cost.
frozen_route_rules.PROBE+REPAIR: Every minimum-cost safe terminal uses REPAIR and at least one probe.
frozen_route_rules.REFUSE: No safe state exists in either capability regime within the frozen 10-probe search space.
frozen_route_rules.MULTI_ROUTE_FRONTIER: Distinct minimum-cost safe terminals realize more than one route type.

preserve_rule: Deleting one probe from an optimal safe terminal is legal only if the resulting coarser representation remains safe under the same capability state.
analysis_boundary: Finite deterministic structural planner test on NASA-simulated aerospace prognostic data. This is not a causal maintenance-policy validation, not an aviation safety recommendation, and not a claim about stochastic or continuous-control optimality.
